title: Retraction of the F11 (s, h) fit and of the 2x local-vs-ranked batching claim
method: re-analysis of the depth sweep already in r1-abba.json plus leg temperatures recovered from r1-harvest.json

claims.derived_claim: local verify batches about half as well as the ranked host, a 2x disagreement
claims.derived_split: head 8.2 percent, target verify 91.8 percent of marginal row cost

what_i_reported_and_now_withdraw.status: WITHDRAWN. The fit is a straight line drawn across a step discontinuity.

root_cause.ledger_text: the true verify cost is a step function of ceil(M/5), which the smooth h/(1+d*h) price cannot express at all
root_cause.independent_confirmation: This sweep was not used by item 92, and it locates the step exactly where item 92 predicts.

per_interval_slopes_arm_all.note: this is the step, not a slope

within_2_pass_band_n2.valid: indicative only, 2 points, no usable intercept

root_cause.why_the_2x_claim_fails: FINDING 286 is fitted where the ranked fixture lives, entirely inside the 2-pass band (rows 5.53-6.78). This sweep has only two points in that band and no usable intercept there. A like-for-like local-vs-ranked (s, h) comparison is therefore not available from this data, in either direction. The 2x figure came from comparing a straddling local fit against a within-band ranked fit.

why_it_must_not_be_proposed.prior_experiment: E25 PRICE arm, hard max depth 3, won 8/8 locally at +3.83 percent
why_it_must_not_be_proposed.governing_rule: a local fixture whose depth histogram does not overlap the ranked one cannot test a depth policy at all, in either direction

this_sweep_fails_that_rule.overlap: none; the local sweep never reaches the scored depth region

depth_policy_near_miss.verdict: not a candidate. This is the E25 local mirage reproduced on a second fixture.

thermal_confound_test.concern: the sweep is ungated and runs depths in strictly ascending order, so depth is confounded with session drift
thermal_confound_test.verdict: refuted. The machine reached thermal steady state from depth 2 onward; drift cannot explain effects of order 1 percent. The sweep data is sound. It is the depth POLICY inference that fails, for the histogram reason above, not for a thermal reason.

corrected_head_share.caveat: the 2-pass slope rests on two points; treat 11-13 percent as the range. The qualitative conclusion is unchanged: the marginal row is dominated by target verify, not by the head.

guardrail_for_finding_286: FINDING 286's linear row law is fitted inside the 2-pass band. It must not be extrapolated below rows = 5, where a verify pass is removed. Any price that multiplies a smooth per-row cost by a depth change which crosses a multiple of 5 rows is wrong by the size of the step.
